evidence.intree_statement: Theorem functor_preserves_split {C D : Category} (F : C ⟶ D) {x y : C} (f g : x ~> y) : SplitCoequalizer f g → SplitCoequalizer (fmap[F] f) (fmap[F] g).

statement_record.book: A Kan extension is ABSOLUTE when it is preserved not merely by the representables (which is pointwiseness) but by ALL functors out of its codomain: postcomposing the extension diagram with any functor whatsoever again yields a Kan extension. Absoluteness therefore strictly strengthens pointwiseness.
statement_record.intree: Theorem functor_preserves_split (F : C ⟶ D) (f g : x ~> y) : SplitCoequalizer f g → SplitCoequalizer (fmap[F] f) (fmap[F] g).  /  Definition preserves_right_Kan `(R : E ⟶ F) := ∀ C D (G : C ⟶ E) (K : C ⟶ D) `(!RightKan K E) `(!RightKan K F), R ◯ Ran K G ≈ Ran K (R ◯ G).
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: the two halves of the book's definition exist separately and never meet. (i) `functor_preserves_split` gives the absoluteness QUANTIFIER (`for every functor F ...`) but only for split coequalizers, stated in the elementary cofork API, never identified with a Kan extension — the in-tree limit/Kan bridge `Kan_Limit` (Structure/Limit/Kan/Extension.v:46) is stated only for limits and Ran, and its colimit/Lan dual is not in the tree, so the absolute split coequalizer is not exhibited as an absolute Lan. (ii) `preserves_right_Kan` is about Kan extensions but has the quantifiers INVERTED relative to absoluteness: it fixes a functor R and quantifies over all extensions, and it demands the extension exist globally on BOTH sides (`!RightKan K E` and `!RightKan K F`). There is no per-extension preservation predicate at all — no `preserves this LocalRightKan` — so the sentence 'this Kan extension is absolute' cannot even be written.

gap: No `Absolute` predicate on a Kan extension exists. What is missing: (a) a LOCAL preservation predicate `H preserves the LocalLeftKan/LocalRightKan (L, eta)` (the in-tree `preserves_left_Kan`/`preserves_right_Kan` are global in the extension and local in the functor — the wrong way round); (b) the definition `absolute := ∀ E (H : D ⟶ E), H preserves this extension`; (c) the comparison with pointwiseness, which cannot be stated either since preservation-by-representables is likewise undefined (grep -rn -i pointwise --include=*.v . returns only comments plus unrelated 'pointwise equivalence' uses). The only in-tree absoluteness result, `functor_preserves_split`, is not connected to the Kan-extension API.
